correctness.rationale: All graph sizes follow from explicit two-colour invariance and a unique solution of 2a=Lambda h sin(a). Both full phase-step increments cancel exactly after two steps. Positive signless-Laplacian Perron vector proves lambda_max=r+s for connected biregular bipartite graphs; the common Jacobian I-h cos(a)L at both phases proves every squared Floquet factor and strict normal contraction/repulsion. Convexity and endpoint equalization prove the unique optimal rate; Taylor expansions prove both edge laws and the scalar critical cubic return. The included script independently passed 92 finite graph/parameter checks. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 model source and follow-up establish small-step Lyapunov and equilibrium results, while the already known weighted bipartite theorem is local near onset and the earlier exact continuation is confined to even cycles. The present theorem proves a new all-parameter, all-mode spectral classification for arbitrary connected biregular bipartite graphs (including noncycle stars and hypercubes), the unique graph-optimal contraction in terms of algebraic connectivity, and a quantified universal neutral upper edge. Comparisons are of mathematical implications, not titles alone; historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating model motivates the question of dynamics beyond the exact Lyapunov step threshold. The global family of canonical period-two orbits, universal sharp parameter window and graph-specific optimal local decay form a meaningful classification for all biregular bipartite networks, not just a degree replacement in one example. The optimum is controlled by algebraic connectivity and produces distinct star and hypercube laws; the all-unit upper Floquet collision has an explicit parabolic scalar return law. General global basin claims are deliberately excluded.
